parts.problem_md:
Most sedimentary rocks are permeable.

Name a sedimentary rock that is:

permeable

impermeable
parts.solution_md:
Permeable: **sandstone**  **[1 mark]**

Impermeable: **shale**  **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **One mark** for a named permeable sedimentary rock (sandstone or limestone)
> - **One mark** for a named impermeable sedimentary rock (shale or clay)

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Both answers must be sedimentary rocks. Granite is igneous and slate is metamorphic, so neither scores here even though they are impermeable.

parts.problem_md:
Most sedimentary rocks are permeable.

Define permeability.
parts.solution_md:
Permeability is the ability of water to pass through a rock or soil  **[1 mark]**, by moving through the pore spaces between its particles  **[1 mark]**.

> **[exam-tip]**
> - A two-mark definition needs two parts: what moves (water) and how it moves (through the pore spaces). Saying only 'lets water through' earns one mark at most.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 1.2 shows terms used in the rock cycle and their descriptions.

![Matching exercise: terms are crystallisation, cementation, erosion and weathering; descriptions cover cooling, transport, compaction, weathering, mineral joining and deposition in layers. Crystallisation is linked to “molten rock cools and solidifies”.](assets/001-matching-exercise-terms-are-crystallisation-ceme.png)

*Figure 1.2*

Draw one line from each term to its correct description.

One line has been done for you.
parts.solution_md:
- Cementation to 'sediments are joined together by minerals' **[1 mark]**
- Weathering to 'break down of rocks into smaller pieces on the surface of the Earth'  **[1 mark]**
- Erosion to 'rock particles are transported by gravity, water, wind and ice'  **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **One mark** for each correct line
> - Draw only one line from each term: an extra line from a term loses the mark for that term

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Two descriptions are left over on purpose. 'Pressed together and water is removed' describes compaction, and 'deposited in layers' describes deposition, so do not join them to any term here.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 1.1 represents the rock cycle.

![Rock cycle diagram: rock A at top, rock B lower right and rock C lower left. Arrows label melting and cooling C to A and B to A, heat and pressure A to B, erosion A to C and B to C, and process X C to B.](assets/002-rock-cycle-diagram-rock-a-at-top-rock-b-lower-ri.png)

*Figure 1.1*

In Figure 1.1, process X changes rock C into rock B.

Circle the correct description of process X.

erosion

heat and pressure

melting and cooling
parts.solution_md:
**heat and pressure**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Rock B is metamorphic rock. Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting, so process X cannot be melting and cooling.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 1.1 represents the rock cycle.

![Rock-cycle diagram with rocks A (top), B (right) and C (left). Arrows show C to A and B to A: “melting and cooling”; A to B: “heat and pressure”; A to C and B to C: “erosion”; C to B: “process X”.](assets/003-rock-cycle-diagram-with-rocks-a-top-b-right-and-.png)

*Figure 1.1*

Identify the rock, A, B or C, that represents igneous rocks in Figure 1.1.
parts.solution_md:
**Rock A**  **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Igneous rock forms when molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies, so look for the rock that the 'melting and cooling' arrows point to.
